title: AWS Tokyo connectivity incident affecting Binance services
positive_signal: Agents that consume market evidence need an explicit way to distinguish healthy, degraded, stale, unavailable and simulated evidence before a recommendation can be treated as actionable.

observed.fact: A connectivity issue in an AWS Tokyo data center disrupted multiple cryptocurrency platforms, including Binance.
Binance said some orders were still succeeding while others were failing during the interruption.
observed.source: Binance public statement as reported by Reuters

observed.fact: Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals for approximately 23 minutes as a safety precaution.

observable_impact: Partial order failures during degraded upstream conditions
inferred_design_lessons: Transport success alone is not evidence quality.
AVAILABLE does not imply FRESH, CONSISTENT or ACTIONABLE.
Partial upstream degradation must reduce evidence coverage instead of being silently converted into confidence.
An agent-facing system must be able to abstain when the evidence contract is not satisfied.
unknown: SignalForge was not running with a captured request trace during the 2025-04-15 incident, so its exact counterfactual output for that event is UNKNOWN.
This record does not claim that SignalForge would have prevented any financial loss during the incident.
The controlled negative-path fixture is a reproduction of the failure class, not a replay of historical Binance payloads.
signalforge_response: Stale or unknown evidence excluded from signal availability
Fail-closed behavior when all usable sources disappear

verification.test_intent: Demonstrate refusal/abstention under degraded evidence without claiming a historical replay.
